statement.essentials: The thin spur of bone called the styloid process lies near the nerve trunk, about a centimetre away on average.
statement.anatomy: The styloid process is one of the bony landmarks measured from the facial nerve trunk: in 40 adult cadavers the shortest distance ranged from 4.3 to 18.6 mm (mean 9.8 mm).

numbers.label: Styloid process to trunk
numbers.design: Micro-dissection, shortest distance to the facial nerve trunk

limitations: One cadaveric series. The styloid is deep and is not itself seen at operation; it is a bony reference measured in specimens.
